messages:
dario: Heads up — saw a ~3x bump in per-token unit cost for the 'mistral-24k' family during last night's canary. Not traffic, tokens/sec was steady. Wondering if it's cache warmup or wrong routing to a higher-cost SKU. Anyone seen this?
jia: yep saw that on the heatmap. cache-hit% dropped right at rollout start. Screenshot: https://img.redwood/test/warmup-spike.png
chris: If it's warmup we should surface that in the cost panel as a transient overlay (projected amortized cost until KV cache warms). Right now the dashboard only shows steady-state numbers which hides rollout spikes.
amelia: telemetry note — we currently sample token events and don't attach route_id to every sample. Without route_id it's hard to attribute cache-hit regressions to a specific canary. Propose adding `route_id` and `model_variant` to the token telemetry event schema. Example event (pseudo):
```
{event: "token_eval", route_id: "r-1234", model_variant: "mistral-24k-v2", cache_hit: false, token_count: 42, sample_weight: 10}
```
katie: UX/quotas question — can we warn on the rollout modal if the estimated unit cost > baseline by X%? Want the PM/dev to see cost risk before starting canary (and optionally auto-throttle or pause).
chris: yeah — rollout modal could show a small card: "Canary cost estimate: $0.012/tk (projected), risk: HIGH" with a checkbox to 'pause on cost surge'. Cost computed from a sliding window of recent token telemetry + warmup model.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started for route r-1234 -> mistral-24k-v2 (canary=10%)
dario: Two actionable asks: 1) add route_id + model_variant to token telemetry samples, 2) add a warmup overlay + canary cost estimate to the cost dashboard and rollout modal. I'll open an RFC.
jia: I'll take the RFC to specing. Quick Q to @amelia — if we attach route_id to samples do we need to change sampling rate during rollouts to keep estimates statistically stable?
amelia: short answer: yes, for the warmup window we should upsample (x4-x8) to reduce variance. We can auto-increase sample_weight for events with `is_canary=true` for 1-3 hours post-deploy. I'll include recommended numbers in the RFC draft.
katie: perfect. Also suggest the console show a short blurb on how amortized cache savings are computed (so PMs don't freak out when transient spikes appear).
dario: great, thanks — I'll file RFC and tag ux/costdash. cc @chris to mock the rollout card.
